annotation.title_clean: Guidelines for Safe Collaborative Robot Design and Implementation
annotation.title_en: Guidelines for Safe Collaborative Robot Design and Implementation
annotation.authors_or_issuer: NSW Government (SafeWork NSW / Centre for Work Health and Safety), Department of Customer Service
annotation.venue: Centre for Work Health and Safety, NSW Government
annotation.summary_en: NSW Government overview of best-practice guidelines for safe collaborative robot (cobot) design and implementation in Australian workplaces. It defines cobots, cobot systems and workplaces, classifies physical, psychological and ethical harms, lists safety measures, and sets five guiding principles, with checklists and risk assessment tools for PCBUs.
key_provisions_or_claims: Cobots are often sold as incomplete machines; end effector and task application determine safety of the complete system.
Hazards classified as physical, psychological and ethical, including collisions, cybersecurity, mental strain and data collection.
Five principles: understand cobot, maintain human focus, align cobot/tool/workspace/workflow, ensure security and protection, support ease of use.
Safety measures cover risk assessment, simulation, physical testing, training and worker co-design.
References AS 4024.3303 (ISO/TS 15066) and ISO 10218 as applicable standards.
